subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the Eduqas spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE Eduqas Chemistry simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Which subatomic particle has a relative charge of +1?
questions.explain: Protons have a relative charge of +1 and a relative mass of 1. Neutrons are neutral; electrons have a charge of -1.

questions.q: Which particle has a negligible mass (about 1/1836 of a proton)?
questions.explain: Electrons have a very small relative mass (often taken as approximately 1/2000), so almost all the mass of an atom is in the nucleus.

questions.q: The atomic number of an element tells you the number of:
questions.explain: The atomic number equals the number of protons. In a neutral atom it also equals the number of electrons.

questions.q: An atom has a mass number of 39 and an atomic number of 19. How many neutrons does it have?
questions.explain: Neutrons = mass number - atomic number = 39 - 19 = 20.

questions.q: A neutral atom has 17 protons and a mass number of 35. How many electrons and neutrons does it have?
questions.explain: A neutral atom has equal protons and electrons (17). Neutrons = 35 - 17 = 18.

questions.q: Where is almost all of the mass of an atom concentrated?
questions.explain: The nucleus contains the protons and neutrons, which have almost all the mass. Electrons contribute negligible mass.

questions.q: Most of the volume of an atom is:
questions.explain: The tiny nucleus is surrounded by electrons in shells, but most of the atom's volume is empty space.

questions.q: The 'plum pudding' model was replaced after which experiment?
questions.explain: Rutherford's alpha-particle (gold foil) scattering experiment showed a small, dense, positive nucleus, disproving the plum pudding model.

questions.q: Which scientist proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed shells or energy levels?
questions.explain: Niels Bohr proposed that electrons occupy fixed energy levels (shells). Chadwick later discovered the neutron.

questions.q: The discovery of the neutron is credited to:
questions.explain: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932, explaining the extra mass in the nucleus.

questions.q: Isotopes of the same element have:
options: The same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
questions.explain: Isotopes have the same number of protons (same element) but different numbers of neutrons, so different mass numbers.

questions.q: Chlorine-35 and chlorine-37 are isotopes. How do their chemical properties compare?
questions.explain: Chemical properties depend on electron arrangement, which is the same for both isotopes, so they react identically. Only physical properties like mass/density differ slightly.

questions.q: An element has two isotopes: 75% of mass 35 and 25% of mass 37. What is its relative atomic mass?
An element has isotopes of mass 63 (69%) and 65 (31%). Its relative atomic mass is closest to:
Relative atomic mass is an average that takes into account:
questions.explain: Relative atomic mass is the weighted mean mass of the isotopes, accounting for how abundant each isotope is.

questions.q: What is the electronic structure of a neutral sodium atom (atomic number 11)?
questions.explain: Shells fill 2, then 8, then 8. Sodium's 11 electrons give 2,8,1 - one electron in the outer shell.

questions.q: An element has electronic structure 2,8,7. Which group of the periodic table is it in?
questions.explain: The number of outer-shell electrons gives the group number. 7 outer electrons means Group 7 (the halogens).

questions.q: A magnesium atom (2,8,2) forms an ion by:
questions.explain: Magnesium loses its 2 outer electrons to gain a full outer shell, forming a 2+ ion (Mg2+).

questions.q: An oxygen atom (2,6) becomes stable by:
questions.explain: Oxygen gains 2 electrons to complete its outer shell (2,8), forming a 2- ion (O2-).

questions.q: The radius of an atom is of the order of:
questions.explain: Atoms have radii around 0.1 nm, which is 1 x 10 to the power -10 metres. The nucleus is around 10,000 times smaller than the atom.
